title: CoralTemp v3.1 has undocumented SST steps in June 1995 (-0.10 C) and July 2002 (+0.09 C) at 35S-35N reefs; they make the 1998 bleaching-level heat-stress extent about 9 points too small
abstract:
Question: NOAA Coral Reef Watch (CRW) v3.1 heat-stress products (HotSpot, Degree Heating Week DHW) use CoralTemp, which joins the OSTIA reanalysis (1985-2002), the Geo-Polar Blended reanalysis (2002-2016) and a near-real-time analysis (from October 2016). The bleaching threshold (MMM) comes from 1985-2012 monthly means, re-centred to 1988.29 with a fitted trend. Is CoralTemp homogeneous at reefs, and do steps change published heat-stress results?
Approach: We compared CoralTemp monthly SST on a 1-degree grid (35S-35N; 574 reef cells) with DOISST v2.1, ERSSTv5, COBE-SST2 and HadSST4.2 (24-month windows, placebo dates, blind break search). Daily CoralTemp at 60 reef cells gave the step days. We re-emulated the CRW climatology (median error 0.00001 C), removed the steps, and re-computed DHW with exact daily CoralTemp (58 cells) and a hybrid daily record (559 cells, 1985-2025).
Results: Relative to all four references, CoralTemp cools by 0.086-0.124 C on about 4 June 1995 (mean -0.105 C, placebo z -7.1) and warms by 0.074-0.099 C on about 15 July 2002 (+0.088 C, z +5.4). Both steps are inside the OSTIA segment and are not documented by CRW. Their dates agree with the start of ATSR-2 data and of the ATSR-2/AATSR overlap. The 1995 step occurs only in the Indo-Pacific. DOISST has no step on these dates. The documented October 2016 merge has no clear step (+0.07 C at reef cells, 0.00 C over 35S-35N, -0.03 C in daily data). Through the MMM re-centring, the steps make operational HotSpots 0.10 C too low at Indo-Pacific reefs from June 1995 to July 2002, and 0.12 C too high at Atlantic-Caribbean reefs after July 2002. With both steps removed, the 1998 share of reef cells at DHW >= 4 increases from 33.6% to 42.5% (40.4-45.3%; exact daily cells 22.4% to 27.6-29.3%). The 2010, 2014-2017 and 2023-2025 extents change by 2 points or less. The ratio of the 2023-2025 extent to the 1998 extent falls from 2.7 to 2.1, and 2023-2025 stays the largest event. The 1985-2025 trend of annual maximum DHW falls by 1-4%, or by 19-20% if the uncertain 2016 step is also removed.
Limitations: The references share in situ data. Grid points are near reefs, not on reef pixels. Box-scale step patterns are not better than noise. The step causes are not proven. Raw CoralTemp data are not redistributed because of the OSTIA terms; code, provenance and aggregate results are included.

Dashed lines: the two large steps (June 1995, 15 July 2002); dotted lines: smaller or uncertain changes. (b-d) Daily CoralTemp minus DOISST at 58 reef cells (7-day mean, 95% band) around the 1995, 2002 and 2016 changes, with the best break day.

(a) Step sizes at reef cells by basin (IP Indo-Pacific, AC Atlantic-Caribbean) for each reference (dots) and their mean (bar). (b) Operational minus homogenised HotSpot by period for variant V2 (1995 and 2002 steps removed): squares are the mean of four references, dots single references.

(a) Yearly share of 559 reef cells with annual maximum DHW >= 4 in the hybrid daily record, operational CRW method against homogenised (V2). (b) Extents of the four global bleaching events; error bars: range of the four references. The 1998 extent increases by about 9 points; later extents change by 2 points or less.
